chapter: Day job, war and Bocage's band
title: Joining Peter Bocage's band: personnel
summary: Around the time of his day job he joined Bocage's six-piece band, whose members he lists and who later left or died.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And did you start working with some other band then, around that time when you started getting a day job? Did you join up any other band then?

Outside of Bocci. You started with Bocci then? Yeah, I started with Bocci. At the same time? Well before I was playing with different bands, you know, spot jobs. And then I started, after Newman died, but Pete hired me.
That was around the same time you started working with your day job?
Yeah, that's around the same time.
And who was in Peter Bocci's band?
Well at the time we started with the bass player, Henry Bocci, Peter Bocci, Charlie Bocci, Lillian Warner, myself, and Alfred Williams, six pieces.
And that band wasn't the reading band anymore? At that time you were more or less just a student. Well they read when he was at the Cadillac.
Oh yeah. At the Cadillac we were at the Realty Tennis. Stuck around us.

Yeah. Did you name the drummer? Yeah, Alfred Williams. After the birthday of the drummer. And then Charlie left the band and went to California and we had John Porter. Big Heavis, you might know him.
